newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firm, sentiment better.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firm, sentiment better.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firmer on Monday, with sentiment a little more cheerful, dealers said.
"Sentiment is a bit better because the Dow closed up on Friday. There is a bit of bargain-hunting going on," said a broker with a local firm.

Dealers said selling of Malaysian stocks traded over the counter also seemed to have slowed. They fell heavily last week after the central bank announced lending curbs for property and stocks. "The selling looks like a bit of an over-reaction. But views are quite mixed with some houses like Sasson calling a sell on Malaysia," said one broker.

After about an hour of trading, the benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index was up 8.24 points to 2,084.02 while the UOB OTC index was up 3.84 points to 1,227.92. Market volume was a light 23 million shares with 130 gainers against 22 losers.
Topping the volume was Malaysia's Arab-Malaysian Development with 1.56 million shares traded, with a block of one million changing hands at S$1.00.
Hong Kong Land was also active and saw block trades of about one million shhares at US$2.33. OUB foreign were also active including several blocks crossed at around S$10.50 a share.
